subject: Linguistics
title: Morphological Creativity
description: A quick, practical guide to Morphological Creativity.

hook.text: Shakespeare invented 'eyeball,' 'lonely,' and 'swagger'—using standard morphological rules.

buildup.text: Speakers create new words constantly by combining morphemes in productive ways.

discovery.text: Advertisers coin words like 'snackable' and 'bingeable'—'-able' keeps working on new roots.

twist.text: Children are morphological prodigies—they create forms like 'unsqueeze' that adults never taught.

climax.text: Morphological creativity shows the system isn't a rigid list—it's a living, generative toolkit.

punchline.text: The rules of word-building never stop building.

quiz.question: Why can children create words like 'unsqueeze'?
options: They memorize every word they hear
